summary: Friedrich Windischmann worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned a doctorate at Bonn under Schlegel, Lassen, and others, and later studied at Munich. He held posts at Munich, Freising, and the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising.

Friedrich Zarncke was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Rostock and at the University of Leipzig under Moriz Haupt and Gottfried Hermann. He later served as privatdozent and rector at Leipzig.

Friedrich von Adelung worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leipzig and later held posts at the School of Oriental Languages in Saint Petersburg, the University of Vienna, and Utrecht University.

Friedrich von Spiegel was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indology scholar. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, Leipzig, and Jena under teachers including Rückert, Lassen, Brockhaus, and Fleischer. He served as professor of Oriental languages at Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University. He held academic posts at Amsterdam, the University of London, the University of Pennsylvania, and as professor at UC Berkeley from 1968 to 1991.

Fritz Burg was an Indologist and scholar in other fields. He earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin before spending his career at the Hamburg State and University Library, serving as Hilfsarbeiter, Sekretär, and finally Bibliothekar (1907–1926).

Fritz Georg Wolff worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the universities of Munich, Heidelberg under Hermann Osthoff, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Giessen, where he completed his Ph.D. under Christian Bartholomae.

Fritz Hommel was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Munich and Leipzig under Friedrich Delitzsch and Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, subsequently holding an academic post at Munich from around 1877 to 1925.

Fritz Johaentgen worked in Indology. He studied at Bonn under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug, and completed his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, later serving as privatdozent there from 1864 to 1878.

Fritz Kern specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Lausanne, Tübingen, and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding professorships at Kiel University, Goethe University Frankfurt (1914–1922), and the University of Bonn (ca. 1925–1947).

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who completed his studies and habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at the University of Bonn, the University of Munich, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz from around 1947 to 1969.

Frédéric Baudry worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Eugène Burnouf and held library positions at the Institut agronomique de Versailles, Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, and Bibliothèque Mazarine.

Frédéric Richard specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Lausanne and the Rangjung Yeshe Institute, later working as coordinator at the University of Lausanne and project manager at the Centre intercantonal d'information sur les croyances.

Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the universities of Strasbourg, Paris, Göttingen, and Humboldt University of Berlin, and subsequently spent his academic career as a professor at the University of Strasbourg from 1840 to 1877.

Frédéric-Gustave Eichhoff specialized in linguistics and Indology. He received his Ph.D. from the University of Paris and later held posts at the Sorbonne and as professor of foreign literature at the University of Lyon from 1842 to 1855.
Fu Yan was a scholar of philosophy and sinology. He studied at the Royal Naval College from around 1877 to 1879 and later held posts at Fudan University and Peking University.

Fu-shih Lin specialized in sinology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser, and held a post at Academia Sinica from 1994 to 2021.

Fuguan Xu worked in philosophy, sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Meiji University and under Shili Xiong, later holding an academic post at Tunghai University from around 1955 to 1969.

Fuhui Zhang works in linguistics, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. Zhang earned a Ph.D. at Northeast Normal University, where they were appointed professor in 2004, and was also affiliated with Tianshui Normal University in 2012.
Fujio Oda is a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Kyushu University and subsequently held academic posts at Beppu University and Fukuoka University.
